- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to compensate.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — apply slight upward bias.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast growth by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×true + 0.3×forecast) for next 3–5 periods.
